title: University of Sydney Demonstrates Multi-Qubit Logical Entanglement and 170-Round Stability on IBM Square-Lattice Nighthawk r2 Processor - Quantum Computing Report
gist: University of Sydney researchers ran distance-3/5 surface code memories (<1% error per round), lattice-surgery logical Bell states (>93% fidelity) and three-logical-qubit teleportation (78-93% process fidelity) on IBM's 120-qubit ibm_phoenix (Nighthawk r2), just 54 days after fleet integration. A 'walking' circuit that alternates data/ancilla roles clears leakage, enabling ~2e-7 error out to 170 rounds.

insights.claim: University of Sydney researchers validated distance-3 and distance-5 rotated surface code memories with under 1% logical error per round on IBM's 120-qubit ibm_phoenix (Nighthawk r2) processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's cloud hardware now supports below-threshold logical memory accessible to external academics.

insights.claim: The team prepared logical Bell states between two planar logical qubits via lattice surgery at over 93% state fidelity, and performed state and gate teleportation across three logical qubits at 78% to 93% process fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QEC on IBM hardware has moved from memory to multi-qubit logic.

insights.claim: The results were the first major multi-qubit logical benchmark on ibm_phoenix, achieved just 54 days after the processor's fleet integration.

insights.claim: Leakage into non-computational transmon states such as |2> accumulates on unmeasured data qubits during stabilizer cycles and saturates error-suppression scaling in multi-round superconducting QEC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Leakage is a primary practical limiter of superconducting QEC scaling.

insights.claim: The Sydney team's 'walking' syndrome circuit alternates data and ancilla roles each round so every physical qubit in the patch is measured and reset every two rounds, clearing leakage before it causes correlated logical faults.
